maria.s: Heads-up: seeing intermittent packet-loss spikes (~0.5-3%) between pods on gpu-pool-3 in us-east-2. Several long-running training jobs hit RTOs around 04:20 UTC. Anyone else seeing this?

infra-bot: [alert] net-loss threshold crossed on node-gpu-12 (gpu-pool-3) at 2026-03-18T04:21:10Z (:warning:)

benji: Yup, saw jitter + retransmits earlier today on that pool. Can you paste ss/tc/qdisc and a small tcpdump so we can narrow whether it's host or overlay?

maria.s: Pasting quick outputs from node-gpu-12 (snipped):
```
$ ss -s
TCP:   1200 (estab 340, closed 560, orphaned 0, synrecv 0, timewait 240/0)
Transport Total     IP        IPv6
RAW     0         0         0
UDP   4200       4200         0
TCP   28000     27000      1000

$ tc qdisc show dev geneve0
qdisc noqueue 0: dev geneve0 state UNKNOWN
qdisc fq_codel 100: parent 1:fff1 limit 10240p

$ ethtool -k eth0 | grep -E "gso|tso|gro"
generic-segmentation-offload: on
tcp-segmentation-offload: on
scatter-gather: on
large-receive-offload: on
```

ashok: Can you run a quick UDP iperf/packetloss test between two affected pods? Also try a 10s ping -s 65000 for MTU stress.

maria.s: I ran ping and a short iperf UDP test between pod A (10.100.4.12) and pod B (10.100.4.45):
```
$ ping -c 100 -s 65000 10.100.4.45
--- 10.100.4.45 ping statistics ---
100 packets transmitted, 97 received, 3% packet loss, time 99501ms

$ iperf3 -c 10.100.4.45 -u -b 5G -t 10
[SUM] 0.00-10.00 sec  4.18 GBytes  3.59 Gbits/sec  31214/1048576 (2.98%)
```

jules: Hmm. 3% loss at MTU-sized ping + UDP loss suggests encapsulation/offload interaction. We had a kernel bump to 5.10.80 on a canary group last night — any overlaps?

benji: Kernel roll happened 03:30 UTC on node-gpu-11/12/13. Could be regression in GSO/GRO handling of Geneve/VXLAN. Check dmesg for mlx5 errors and look for "net_ratelimit" lines. Also capture encapsulated packets on the host: `tcpdump -ni eth0 'udp and port 6081' -w /tmp/encap.pcap`

maria.s: tcpdump snippet from host capturing encapsulated frames (showing retransmits):
```
15:04:20.123456 IP 10.0.3.45.40123 > 10.0.3.12.52012: UDP, length 1420
15:04:20.123789 IP 10.100.4.12.50052 > 10.100.4.45.50052: Flags [P.], seq 12345:12489, ack 9876, win 29200, length 144
15:04:20.124001 IP 10.100.4.12.50052 > 10.100.4.45.50052: Flags [.], ack 9876, win 29200, length 0 (retransmission)
```

ashok: Try disabling GSO/GRO on the host as a fast repro/fix: `ethtool -K eth0 gso off gro off tso off`. If loss disappears, likely offload bug in NIC/kernel path. Also confirm Geneve offload flags with `ip -d link show geneve0`.

deploy-bot: rolling kubelet restart initiated on nodes node-gpu-11,node-gpu-12 at 2026-03-18T05:00:00Z

jules: I'm going to drain node-gpu-12 and repro with GSO toggled. If toggling clears it, we should pin kernel or file vendor bug with capture and kernel config.

maria.s: Update: drained node-gpu-12 -> traffic rebalanced to node-gpu-11/13. Observed loss drop to ~0.1% on flows that moved, but node-gpu-11 still has spikes. Toggling offloads on node-gpu-11 temporarily removed spikes. Saving captures at /var/tmp/encap-traces/ for share.

benji: Great repro. Next steps: collect `ethtool -k` on affected nodes, `dmesg | tail -n 200`, and full pcap of encapsulated traffic. I'll open incident DC-243 and attach traces + kernel/git-match. Also assign vendor mlx5 ticket if we confirm hw offload issue. :+1:

maria.s: added ethtool/dmesg/pcap to the incident folder and labeled DC-243 as "vxlan/geneve-offload-suspect". Thanks all — will keep thread updated.
